newsitem.title: USA: Repeal of US Humphrey-Hawkins law proposed.
newsitem.headline: Repeal of US Humphrey-Hawkins law proposed.

text.p: Two U.S. Republican lawmakers said on Wednesday said they plan to reintroduce legislation to repeal the Humphrey-Hawkins law and replace it with a requirement that the Fed to have the single goal of seeking price stability.
Humphrey-Hawkins legislation has the twin goals of price stability and full employment.
"We believe that the best way to promote economic growth and jobs is to create an environment that fosters a stable and prosperous economy," Senator Connie Mack of Florida said.
Mack is vice chairman and Jim Saxon of New Jersey is chairman of Joint Economic Committee of Congress.
Their statement followed a semi-annual report to Congress on the state of the economy by Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan, also required under the Humphrey-Hawkins legislation.
